animals_giraffe_height_0001.claim: Which land animal is the tallest? Answer: Giraffe. Its long neck and legs help a giraffe reach high branches.

animals_giraffe_neck_0001.claim: How many neck vertebrae does a giraffe normally have? Answer: 7. The number matches humans, but each vertebra is much longer.

animals_giraffe_relative_0001.claim: Which animal is the giraffe’s closest living relative? Answer: Okapi. The okapi and giraffe belong to the giraffe family.

animals_cheetah_sprint_0001.claim: Which land mammal runs fastest over a short distance? Answer: Cheetah. Cheetahs are sprinters and cannot sustain their top speed for long.

animals_cheetah_tail_0001.claim: What helps a cheetah steer while running fast? Answer: A long tail. The tail acts as a rudder to help the animal maintain direction.

animals_panda_diet_0001.claim: Which plant makes up most of a giant panda’s diet? Answer: Bamboo. Pandas eat shoots and leaves, peeling the tough outer layers from stalks.

animals_panda_thumb_0001.claim: What forms a giant panda’s “false thumb”? Answer: An enlarged wrist bone. This bone helps pandas grasp and manipulate bamboo stalks.

animals_platypus_eggs_0001.claim: Which of these mammals lays eggs? Answer: Platypus. Platypuses are monotremes and feed their young with milk.

animals_platypus_bill_0001.claim: Which signals does a platypus’s bill detect when it searches for prey? Answer: Electrical impulses. Electroreceptors help locate prey while its eyes are closed underwater.

animals_platypus_habitat_0001.claim: In what kind of water do platypuses usually forage? Answer: Fresh water. They live mainly in streams, rivers, lakes and ponds.

dinosaurs_triceratops_name_0001.claim: What does the name Triceratops mean? Answer: Three-horned face. Two horns were above the eyes and another was on the nose.

dinosaurs_triceratops_diet_0001.claim: What did Triceratops eat? Answer: Plants. Its beak and shearing teeth helped it process tough vegetation.

dinosaurs_stegosaurus_defence_0001.claim: What weapon did Stegosaurus use against predators? Answer: Tail spikes. Its powerful spiked tail could deter an attacker.

dinosaurs_stegosaurus_period_0001.claim: In which geological period did Stegosaurus live? Answer: Jurassic. Stegosaurus lived in the Late Jurassic, long before the end of the Cretaceous.

dinosaurs_stegosaurus_plates_0001.claim: Where were the bony plates of Stegosaurus located? Answer: In the skin along its back. The plates were not attached directly to the rest of its skeleton.

dinosaurs_living_dinosaurs_0001.claim: Which living group of animals belongs to the dinosaurs? Answer: Birds. Birds are the surviving branch of the dinosaur family tree.

dinosaurs_pterosaurs_group_0001.claim: Which group did pterosaurs belong to? Answer: Flying reptiles. Pterosaurs were archosaurs, but they were not dinosaurs.

dinosaurs_dinosaur_stance_0001.claim: What limb position is characteristic of dinosaurs? Answer: Beneath the body. An upright stance distinguishes them from many other reptiles.

dinosaurs_velociraptor_origin_0001.claim: In which of these countries have Velociraptor fossils been found? Answer: Mongolia. This small carnivorous theropod lived in the Late Cretaceous.

dinosaurs_dimetrodon_0001.claim: Which of these animals was not a dinosaur? Answer: Dimetrodon. Dimetrodon belonged to a different evolutionary branch and lived before dinosaurs.

video_games_ps1_japan_year_0001.claim: In which year was the original PlayStation released in Japan? Answer: 1994. North America and Europe received the console the following year.

video_games_ps1_disc_0001.claim: Which medium carried games for the original PlayStation? Answer: CD-ROM. Optical discs could hold more data than contemporary cartridges.

video_games_ps1_chip_0001.claim: Which CPU did the original PlayStation use? Answer: R3000. It was a 32-bit processor used for tasks including 3D graphics.

video_games_ps2_japan_year_0001.claim: In which year did PlayStation 2 go on sale in Japan? Answer: 2000. It launched in Japan in March and in Europe in November of the same year.

video_games_ps2_dvd_0001.claim: Which video format could PlayStation 2 play without a separate player? Answer: DVD. Built-in movie playback made the console a home multimedia device.

video_games_ps2_cpu_0001.claim: What was the CPU of PlayStation 2 called? Answer: Emotion Engine. The processor helped produce complex game imagery for its era.

video_games_ps2_slim_0001.claim: What was the thinner PlayStation 2 model released in 2004 called? Answer: PS2 Slim. The smaller model included an Ethernet port for online play.

video_games_ps2_network_0001.claim: Which accessory enabled early PS2 models to connect online? Answer: Network Adaptor. The adapter fitted at the back and provided a network connection.

video_games_guitar_hero_debut_0001.claim: On which console did the Guitar Hero series begin in 2005? Answer: PlayStation 2. The music game let players perform rock tracks using a guitar controller.

video_games_singstar_play_0001.claim: Which accessory do players use in the karaoke series SingStar? Answer: Microphone. The series scored players’ vocal performances of familiar songs.

cartoons_woody_toy_0001.claim: What kind of toy is Woody in Toy Story? Answer: Cowboy. Woody has a pull-string voice box.

cartoons_buzz_role_0001.claim: What does Buzz Lightyear believe himself to be at the start of Toy Story? Answer: A space ranger. He believes he is on a mission for Star Command.

cartoons_nemo_father_0001.claim: What is Nemo’s father’s name? Answer: Marlin. His father travels across the ocean to bring him home.

cartoons_nemo_species_0001.claim: What kind of fish are Nemo and Marlin? Answer: Clownfish. Their home is an anemone on the Great Barrier Reef.

cartoons_remy_species_0001.claim: What animal is Remy in Ratatouille? Answer: Rat. He dreams of becoming a chef despite people’s attitudes toward rodents.

cartoons_ratatouille_city_0001.claim: In which city does Remy pursue his dream of becoming a chef? Answer: Paris. He finds himself beneath the restaurant of his hero Auguste Gusteau.

cartoons_monsters_factory_0001.claim: What does the factory process at the beginning of Monsters, Inc.? Answer: Children’s screams. Sulley’s job involves visiting children’s bedrooms.

cartoons_monsters_boo_0001.claim: What does Sulley call the girl who enters the monster world? Answer: Boo. A human child’s arrival disrupts the usual life of Monstropolis.

cartoons_walle_job_0001.claim: What task was WALL-E built to perform? Answer: Clean up trash. The robot compacts waste left on Earth into cubes.

cartoons_walle_eve_0001.claim: What is the name of the probe robot WALL-E meets? Answer: EVE. She searches for evidence that Earth can support life again.

literature_pride_author_0001.claim: Who wrote Pride and Prejudice? Answer: Jane Austen. The story centers on Elizabeth and her relationship with Mr. Darcy.

literature_pride_family_0001.claim: What is Elizabeth’s family name in Pride and Prejudice? Answer: Bennet. Elizabeth is one of five daughters in the family.

literature_alice_author_0001.claim: Who wrote Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland? Answer: Lewis Carroll. The adventure begins with an unusual rabbit carrying a watch.

literature_alice_rabbit_0001.claim: Whom does Alice follow down the rabbit hole? Answer: The White Rabbit. Alice notices the watch the rabbit takes from his waistcoat pocket.

literature_frankenstein_author_0001.claim: Who wrote the novel Frankenstein? Answer: Mary Shelley. The novel’s subtitle refers to the myth of Prometheus.

literature_frankenstein_creator_0001.claim: What is the name of the scientist who creates a living being in Shelley’s novel? Answer: Victor Frankenstein. Frankenstein is the creator’s surname, not the creature’s personal name.

literature_moby_author_0001.claim: Who wrote Moby-Dick? Answer: Herman Melville. The voyage is narrated by the sailor Ishmael.

literature_moby_ship_0001.claim: What is the name of Captain Ahab’s whaling ship? Answer: Pequod. The crew sails aboard it in pursuit of the white whale.

literature_holmes_author_0001.claim: Who created Sherlock Holmes? Answer: Arthur Conan Doyle. Many stories about the detective are narrated by his friend Watson.

literature_watson_profession_0001.location: A Scandal in Bohemia: civil practice
literature_watson_profession_0001.claim: What is the profession of Holmes’s friend Dr. Watson? Answer: Physician. Early in the collection, Watson mentions returning to medical practice.

ecology_compost_process_0001.claim: What happens to organic waste during composting? Answer: Aerobic microbial decomposition. The resulting material can be used to improve soil.

ecology_compost_oxygen_0001.claim: Which gas is needed for ordinary aerobic composting? Answer: Oxygen. Microorganisms also need water and nutrients.

ecology_vermicompost_0001.claim: Which animals help produce vermicompost? Answer: Worms. This is one way to process food scraps at home.

ecology_compost_water_0001.claim: How does adding compost affect the soil’s ability to retain water? Answer: Increases water-holding capacity. The soil becomes more resilient during drought and heavy rainfall.

ecology_ozone_layer_0001.claim: Which radiation does the ozone layer help protect us from? Answer: Ultraviolet. Ozone is especially important for absorbing UVB radiation.

ecology_ozone_stratosphere_0001.claim: Which atmospheric layer contains most atmospheric ozone? Answer: Stratosphere. It lies above the troposphere, where most weather occurs.

ecology_ozone_atoms_0001.claim: How many oxygen atoms are in an ozone molecule? Answer: 3. Its molecular structure differs from ordinary two-atom oxygen.

ecology_greenhouse_gas_0001.claim: Which of these is a greenhouse gas? Answer: Carbon dioxide. Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere.

ecology_landfill_methane_0001.claim: Which greenhouse gas is produced when organic waste decays in landfills? Answer: Methane. Landfills are one source of emissions of this gas.

ecology_plant_carbon_0001.claim: Which process uses carbon dioxide to form organic matter in plants? Answer: Photosynthesis. The carbon becomes part of the plants’ organic material.

architecture_taj_material_0001.claim: Which stone forms the main structure of the Taj Mahal? Answer: White marble. The mausoleum stands in the Indian city of Agra.

architecture_taj_patron_0001.claim: Which ruler commissioned the Taj Mahal? Answer: Shah Jahan. The building commemorates his wife.

architecture_taj_function_0001.claim: What was the principal purpose of the Taj Mahal? Answer: Mausoleum. The monument belongs to the architecture of the Mughal Empire.

architecture_sydney_architect_0001.claim: Whose design was chosen for the Sydney Opera House? Answer: Jørn Utzon. The Danish architect won the international competition in 1957.

architecture_sydney_opening_0001.claim: In which year was the Sydney Opera House inaugurated? Answer: 1973. The building became a major work of twentieth-century architecture.

architecture_sydney_roof_0001.claim: Which forms make up the famous roof of the Sydney Opera House? Answer: Vaulted shells. The shells are grouped over the halls and a restaurant.

architecture_jerusalem_dome_0001.claim: In which century was the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem built? Answer: 7th. The monument’s decoration includes geometric and floral motifs.

architecture_kathmandu_groups_0001.claim: How many monument zones form UNESCO’s Kathmandu Valley property? Answer: 7. The property includes palace squares, Buddhist stupas and Hindu temples.

architecture_kathmandu_stupa_0001.claim: Which of these Kathmandu Valley monuments is a Buddhist stupa? Answer: Bauddhanath. UNESCO lists Bauddhanath alongside the Swayambhu stupa.

architecture_taj_century_0001.claim: In which century was the Taj Mahal built? Answer: 17th. UNESCO dates construction of the mausoleum to 1631–1648.

painting_nighthawks_author_0001.claim: Who painted Nighthawks? Answer: Edward Hopper. The painting dates to 1942.

painting_nighthawks_medium_0001.claim: Which medium did Edward Hopper use for Nighthawks? Answer: Oil on canvas. The work belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago collection.

painting_bedroom_author_0001.claim: Who painted The Bedroom held by the Art Institute of Chicago? Answer: Vincent van Gogh. The Chicago version of the painting dates to 1889.

painting_bedroom_date_0001.claim: What is the date of the Chicago version of Van Gogh’s The Bedroom? Answer: 1889. It is an oil painting on canvas.

painting_grande_jatte_author_0001.claim: Who painted A Sunday on La Grande Jatte? Answer: Georges Seurat. The main painting dates to 1884–1886.

painting_grande_jatte_technique_0001.location: Description: dots, dashes and pointillist technique
painting_grande_jatte_technique_0001.claim: Which technique characterizes Seurat’s A Sunday on La Grande Jatte? Answer: Pointillism. Dots and short strokes of color combine into forms when seen from a distance.

painting_american_gothic_author_0001.claim: Who painted American Gothic? Answer: Grant Wood. The painting was created in 1930.

painting_american_gothic_daughter_0001.location: Description: farmer and his daughter; rural values
painting_american_gothic_daughter_0001.claim: According to the museum, how is the woman related to the farmer in American Gothic? Answer: Daughter. Wood wanted to convey traditional rural American values.

painting_water_lilies_author_0001.claim: Who painted the 1906 Water Lilies in the Art Institute of Chicago? Answer: Claude Monet. This work is painted in oil on canvas.

painting_water_lilies_garden_0001.claim: In which French village was Monet’s garden that inspired his Water Lilies? Answer: Giverny. The artist created a water garden there with a pond and Japanese bridge.
